entries.appliesTo: residential rental property owners (and their agents/subcontractors) and owners of rent-pricing coordinators (software, data analytics services, or entities performing a coordinating function)

exposure.enforcer: NJ Antitrust Act §§ 7-17 remedies (incl. attorney-general and private actions under that act)

sources.prohibition: § 3 — 'It shall be unlawful and a violation of the "New Jersey Antitrust Act," P.L.1970, c.73 (C.56:9-1 et seq.) for: a. a rental property owner, or any agent, representative, or subcontractor thereof … to subscribe to, contract with, or otherwise exchange any form of consideration in return for the use of services of a coordinator; b. the owner of a coordinator to facilitate an agreement among rental property owners that restricts competition with respect to residential dwelling units, including by performing a coordinating function; … c. two or more rental property owners to engage in consciously parallel pricing coordination'
sources.enforcer: § 4 — 'Sections 7 through 17 of the "New Jersey Antitrust Act," P.L.1970, c.73 (C.56:9-7 through 56:9-17) shall apply for a violation pursuant to section 3 of this act.'

flags: text on file is the First Reprint (Amended 2026-03-10); LegiScan lists later versions (Comm Sub 2026-06-09, Amended 2026-06-24) that extracted to 0 chars — final enacted text may differ from what was coded
enforcement routed through cross-referenced NJ Antitrust Act §§ 7-17 (rule 4: no penaltyMax coded from this text)
AI/algorithm nexus is in the 'coordinating function' definition: 'analyzing or processing nonpublic information through use of a system, software, algorithm, or other automated process' (§ 2)
relaxed pleading standard for § 3 claims: complaint 'need not allege facts tending to exclude the possibility of independent action' (§ 5.a(2)), limited to this act's violations only (§ 5.b)

carve-outs: licensed real estate brokers/salespersons (§§ 2, 3.a), aggregated-data reports and research/testing uses (§ 2), government rental price restriction programs (§ 2), multiple listing services and their members (§ 7), third-party property managers acting under a rental contract (§ 8), single-owner multi-property actions (§ 2)

non-company provisions: state public education program duty on Department of Law and Public Safety and Department of Community Affairs (§ 9), AG/Commissioner rulemaking (§ 10), municipal-ordinance preemption (§ 6.b) — noted here per category rule
effective 'the first day of the fourth month next following the date of enactment' (§ 11)
